Elena: Quick post-all-hands clarification request: leadership mentioned 'supply hedging' for GPU procurement and a new "soft-failover" path. Can someone spell out what that means for customer latency and routing?

Marcus: Short version: supply hedging = keeping a mix of on-demand, reserved, and spot-backed capacity plus prewarm pools so we can absorb procurement variance. Soft-failover is automated routing that prefers cheaper/quantized variants or nearby regions before triggering hard failover (burst buckets or contracted capacity).

Zoe: For customers: the visible differences are small for short spikes (maybe +50-150ms p99), larger if sustained (up to ~400ms if we cross-region). We try to avoid token-quality impact by preferring quantized model variants with verified fidelity.

Tariq: Ops note: there is a short playbook we're using for soft-failover, publishing here so PMs/CS can quote it. Full runbook is incoming.

```# soft-failover quick flow
if region.capacity < threshold:
  1) route -> quantized_variant (same model family)
  2) enable_small_batches()
  3) try_local_prewarm(timeout=2m)
  4) if still constrained -> route_to_adjacent_region()
  5) notify #infra #support #cs
```

Elena: Nice. Can we get concrete thresholds and a short customer-facing blurb we can paste into emails/status pages?

Marcus: Thresholds: prewarm headroom < 15% triggers soft-failover. Sustained < 5% for 10m triggers burst bucket remapping. Blurb: "If regional prewarm runs low, we'll route to optimized model variants or nearby capacity to preserve responsiveness; you may see small latency increases while we remain within SLA. If pressure persists, we'll use reserved burst capacity or cross-region failover."

InfraBot: Runbook page created: https://confluence.redwood/infra/soft-failover-runbook :white_check_mark:

Elena: Thanks everyone 1 — I'll coordinate with CS to push a short FAQ and attach the runbook link. :thumbsup:
